mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates economic weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strong demand in the economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased consistently over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month indicates supply chain disruptions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO dropped by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals an inflationary pressure without adequate monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month AND FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in a month and FEDFUNDS was below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 in 1 month AND UNRATE increase > 0.3%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 and UNRATE increased by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals strong consumer demand and a robust labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month AND UNRATE decrease > 0.2%
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and robust labor market
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased consistently over two consecutive quarters.
